results.cause: The deployment runs image "busybox:1.36" with command ["/app/payment-gateway","--listen=:8443"], but busybox does not contain that binary: "exec: \"/app/payment-gateway\": stat /app/payment-gateway: no such file or directory" (StartError, exit 128). The rule finding mentions exit 127, but here runc fails before the process starts, so the code is 128. The cause is the same: the image is likely wrong (a placeholder busybox instead of the payment-gateway app image), or the command path is wrong.
fix: Set spec.template.spec.containers[name=gateway].image in deployment/payment-gateway to the actual payment-gateway application image that contains /app/payment-gateway, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/payment-gateway gateway=<your-payment-gateway-image:tag>
If the image is correct but the binary lives elsewhere, change containers[gateway].command to the real binary path in that image (check with: docker run --rm --entrypoint ls <image> -l /app).
After fixing, the Deployment will roll out a new ReplicaSet; check with kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/payment-gateway (it currently shows ProgressDeadlineExceeded).

results.cause: Migration 0042_add_orders_index tries to create an index that already exists: the log says "ERROR: relation "orders_idx" already exists" and the container exits 1. In this pod the init container's args are a script that echoes that error and runs a hard-coded "exit 1", so it can never succeed as written. Either the script is a deliberate failing placeholder, or in the real app the migration is not idempotent and orders_idx was already created (for example by an earlier partial run).
fix: If this is the real migration, make it idempotent (e.g. CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS orders_idx ...), or mark 0042 as already applied in the migration tracking table, since orders_idx already exists.
Fix the init container script in the Deployment spec (spec.template.spec.initContainers[name=migrate].args): remove the hard-coded 'exit 1' and run the actual migration command.

Apply the change with kubectl apply -f <manifest> (or kubectl edit deployment/orders-api -n pfa-lab), then run kubectl rollout status deployment/orders-api -n pfa-lab to confirm the init container completes and api starts.

results.cause: The app refuses its config: MAX_CONNECTIONS is set to "ten" and the app needs an integer, so it logs level=fatal msg="config: MAX_CONNECTIONS=\"ten\" is not an integer" and exits 1. The redis:6379 and statsd:8125 connection-refused errors are not the cause. Redis falls back to in-memory, and the statsd flush failure happens during shutdown.
fix: Set the MAX_CONNECTIONS env var on container api to an integer (for example "10" instead of "ten"), either in the Deployment spec or in the ConfigMap/Secret it comes from.
Roll out again: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/pricing-api (only needed if the value came from a ConfigMap/Secret; editing the Deployment spec rolls out automatically).
Optional and separate from this crash: check that the redis service (CACHE_URL) and statsd:8125 (STATSD_ADDR) are reachable in pfa-lab, so the app gets a shared cache and metrics.

results.cause: The startup script requires DATABASE_URL and exits 1 when it is empty; the container only has env vars DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and LOG_LEVEL, so the log shows "FATAL: required environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set". Separately, the script echoes the DB password to the logs (a password value was present and redacted).
fix: Add DATABASE_URL to spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env in deployment/checkout-api, preferably via valueFrom.secretKeyRef since it likely contains credentials, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set env deployment/checkout-api --from=secret/<your-db-secret> --keys=DATABASE_URL (or edit the manifest and kubectl apply).
Let the rollout create a new pod and verify with: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/checkout-api
Remove the 'echo "db config: user=$DB_USER password=$DB_PASSWORD"' line from the container args so the password is not written to logs, and rotate that password since it has been logged.

results.cause: DB_HOST is set to "orders-db" and DNS lookup fails: "FATAL: db: dial tcp: lookup orders-db on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host". The startup script exits 1 when nslookup fails, so there is most likely no Service named orders-db in namespace pfa-lab, or it lives in another namespace and needs the qualified name (orders-db.<namespace>).
fix: Check whether the Service exists: kubectl get svc orders-db -n pfa-lab (and kubectl get svc -A | grep orders-db to find it in another namespace).
If it is missing, deploy the Postgres database and its Service named orders-db in pfa-lab.

If it is in another namespace or has a different name, update the DB_HOST env var on deployment/shipping-api to the correct name, e.g. orders-db.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local: kubectl set env deployment/shipping-api -n pfa-lab DB_HOST=<correct-host>

results.cause: The api startup script requires REDIS_URL and exits 1 when it is empty. The log says "FATAL: required environment variable REDIS_URL is not set", and the container only defines env var "PORT". Separately, the worker container exits with code 2 because "/etc/cart/worker.yaml" does not exist. It has no volume mounted there, only the serviceaccount token mount. Both must be fixed for the pod to become Ready.
fix: Add REDIS_URL to the api container in deployment/cart-service (spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].env). If it holds credentials, use valueFrom.secretKeyRef, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab create secret generic cart-redis --from-literal=REDIS_URL=<url>, then reference that key.

For the worker container, create a ConfigMap containing worker.yaml (kubectl -n pfa-lab create configmap cart-worker-config --from-file=worker.yaml). Add it as a volume and mount it at /etc/cart in the worker container (volumeMounts mountPath: /etc/cart).
Apply the updated Deployment and check the rollout: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/cart-service.

results.cause: Docker Hub answers "docker.io/library/busybox:1.36.1-uclbic: not found" (rpc error code = NotFound). The tag does not exist, almost certainly a typo: "uclbic" should be "uclibc" (busybox publishes uclibc variant tags such as 1.36.1-uclibc).
fix: Correct the image tag: kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/storefront web=busybox:1.36.1-uclibc
Also fix the tag in the source manifest/Helm values (spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image) so the next apply doesn't revert it
Verify the tag exists before rolling out, e.g. `docker manifest inspect busybox:1.36.1-uclibc`, then watch with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/storefront`

results.cause: The image field contains two tags (":1.36" and ":latest"). A reference allows only one tag, so the kubelet rejects it with "couldn't parse image name \"busybox:1.36:latest\": invalid reference format" (InvalidImageName). The registry is never contacted.
fix: Set the container image to a single tag, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/notify-worker worker=busybox:1.36`, or change `spec.template.spec.containers[name=worker].image` to "busybox:1.36" in the manifest.
If the image string is built from variables (e.g. a templated tag), fix the template so it doesn't append ":latest" to a value that already has a tag.

Confirm the rollout with `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/notify-worker`. The deployment hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded, and the new ReplicaSet will start progressing again after the change.

results.cause: The tag does not exist: the registry answered "docker.io/library/busybox:1.63: not found" (code = NotFound). "1.63" is not a published busybox tag, so it is likely a typo or a wrong version. There is also a secondary warning, "Unable to retrieve some image pull secrets (regcred)". The pod references an imagePullSecret "regcred" that does not exist in pfa-lab. Public busybox does not need it, and the error is NotFound, not unauthorized, so it is not the cause.
fix: Change spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image in deployment/admin-portal to a busybox tag that exists, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/admin-portal web=busybox:<valid-tag>`. Check available tags with `crane ls busybox` or on Docker Hub first.
Confirm the rollout succeeds: `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/admin-portal`.

Clean up the pull secret warning. Either remove "regcred" from spec.template.spec.imagePullSecrets, since public busybox needs no credentials, or create the secret in namespace pfa-lab if it is required for other images.

results.cause: Pulls go through the mirror at registry-mirror:1273, and it answered the manifest HEAD request with "500 Internal Server Error" for registry.pfa-lab.invalid/billing/ui:3.2.0. A 500 means the mirror failed to fetch from upstream; it is not a 'not found' or 'unauthorized' answer. The upstream hostname "registry.pfa-lab.invalid" uses the reserved .invalid TLD, which never resolves in DNS, so the image reference most likely points to a wrong or placeholder registry host. The mirror itself failing is the less likely explanation.
fix: Correct the registry host in the Deployment's container image (spec.template.spec.containers[name=web].image) to the real registry, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab set image deployment/billing-ui web=<real-registry>/billing/ui:3.2.0

If registry.pfa-lab.invalid is intentionally the upstream, configure the mirror registry-mirror:1273 so it can resolve and reach that host (fix its upstream/DNS settings), or bypass the mirror for this registry in the node's containerd config
If the upstream is correct and reachable, check the mirror registry-mirror:1273 itself; its logs should show why it returns 500
After fixing, roll out again (kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/billing-ui), since the Deployment shows ProgressDeadlineExceeded

results.cause: The container command runs `stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 300M --vm-hang 0`, which allocates 300M, but resources.limits.memory is 200Mi. The logs show the process reach 'cache warmup: loading remaining 100MB' and 'dispatching hogs: ... 1 vm', and then it is OOMKilled (exit code 137). The workload needs more memory than the limit allows, so this is not a leak.
fix: Raise resources.limits.memory (and requests.memory) on container cache in statefulset/session-cache to at least 384Mi, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset session-cache --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"384Mi"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/memory","value":"384Mi"}]'`. This leaves headroom over the 300M allocation.
Alternatively, reduce usage to fit the 200Mi limit: lower `--vm-bytes 300M` in the container args to well below 200Mi, e.g. 150M.
If the pod does not pick up the new spec, delete it so the StatefulSet recreates it: `kubectl -n pfa-lab delete pod session-cache-0`.

results.cause: The container deliberately allocates about 250MB ('exec stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 250M --vm-hang 0'; log: 'loading 250MB of order history into memory'), roughly twice its memory limit of 128Mi. Each run ends with 'OOMKilled', exit code 137, within the same second it started (14:54:50).
fix: Raise the memory limit above the 250M working set plus overhead in the deployment's container 'worker': set resources.limits.memory to 384Mi and resources.requests.memory to at least 256Mi (for example, kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/report-worker -c worker --limits=memory=384Mi --requests=memory=256Mi).

Alternatively, if 128Mi must stay, reduce what the app loads at once: lower --vm-bytes (or the real app's batch or cache size) to well under 128M, for example 96M, by processing the order history in chunks.
After the change, watch the rollout with kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/report-worker and confirm usage with kubectl -n pfa-lab top pod.

results.cause: The container runs "stress --vm 1 --vm-bytes 200M --vm-hang 0" (log: "log-shipper starting, buffering 200MB of logs in memory"), so it tries to hold 200M of memory, but resources.limits.memory is 64Mi. The kernel kills it right away: last state OOMKilled, exit code 137, started and finished at 2026-11-11T14:54:20. The 128Mi suggested by the generic rule would still be too low for a 200M allocation.
fix: Make the workload fit the limit: lower the buffer in the log-shipper args, e.g. change --vm-bytes 200M to a value well under 64Mi (such as 32M), or cap the shipper's in-memory buffer to that size.
Or, if the shipper really needs to buffer 200MB, raise the log-shipper container's resources.limits.memory and resources.requests.memory to about 256Mi so 200M plus overhead fits.

Apply the change, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab edit deployment/search-api or kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/search-api -c log-shipper --limits=memory=256Mi --requests=memory=256Mi, then confirm the pod becomes Ready.

results.cause: Container trainer requests cpu "4k" (4000 whole cores), which is almost certainly a unit typo for "4000m" (4 cores). The only node cannot offer 4000 cores, so the scheduler reports "0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient cpu" and preemption cannot help.
fix: In deployment/ml-trainer, set spec.template.spec.containers[name=trainer].resources.requests.cpu to "4000m", or to the smaller value the trainer really needs, e.g.: kubectl -n pfa-lab set resources deployment/ml-trainer -c trainer --requests=cpu=4000m

Keep the request within the node's allocatable CPU (check with kubectl describe node). If the node has fewer than 4 allocatable cores, lower the request further (the workload only runs 'sleep 3600') or add a larger node.
After the rollout, confirm the new pod is scheduled: kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/ml-trainer

results.cause: The pod's volume "templates" references configmap "email-templates", which does not exist in namespace pfa-lab. The FailedMount event has repeated 1075 times since 2026-11-02T15:26:39, and the Deployment has hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Create the missing configmap in the namespace, e.g. `kubectl -n pfa-lab create configmap email-templates --from-file=<templates-dir>`, or apply its manifest if it lives elsewhere in your repo.
If the configmap exists under a different name, fix the configMap.name of volume "templates" in deployment/email-sender (spec.template.spec.volumes) to match it.
If the templates are optional, set `optional: true` on the configMap volume source so the pod can start without it.
After the configmap exists, the kubelet retries the mount automatically. Alternatively, run `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/email-sender`.

results.cause: The pod spec sets nodeSelector {"hardware": "gpu-a100"}, and the only node in the cluster doesn't carry that label: "0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." Preemption can't help, so the pod will never schedule as-is.
fix: If the workload doesn't need an A100 node (the container is busybox:1.36 running 'sleep 3600'), remove the selector: kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment video-encoder --type=json -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
If it should run on a specific node, check its labels with 'kubectl get nodes --show-labels' and set spec.template.spec.nodeSelector to a label that node actually has.
If the node really is the intended GPU node but is missing the label, add it: kubectl label node <node-name> hardware=gpu-a100
Otherwise, add a node labeled hardware=gpu-a100 to the cluster.

results.cause: PVC metrics-data requests storageClassName "fast-ssd", but that StorageClass does not exist: ProvisioningFailed "storageclass.storage.k8s.io \"fast-ssd\" not found" (x102). No volume is provisioned, so the scheduler reports "pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims" and the Deployment hit ProgressDeadlineExceeded.
fix: Run `kubectl get storageclass` to see which StorageClasses exist (and which is default).

Delete and recreate PVC metrics-data in namespace pfa-lab with spec.storageClassName set to an existing class (storageClassName is immutable on an existing claim): `kubectl -n pfa-lab delete pvc metrics-data`, then apply the corrected manifest (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce).
Alternatively, create a StorageClass named fast-ssd backed by a provisioner available in this cluster.
Once the claim is Bound, the pending pod will schedule. If the Deployment stays stuck, run `kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout restart deployment/metrics-store`.

results.cause: The readiness check depends on the database host in DB_HOST, which is set to inventory-db, and that name does not resolve: logs show "readiness: database inventory-db:5432 unreachable: lookup inventory-db: no such host". There is likely no Service named inventory-db in namespace pfa-lab, or it lives in another namespace and needs the namespace-qualified name. The probe itself is correct: port http=80 and path /cgi-bin/ready match what the app serves. The single 'connection refused' event was only at startup, before httpd was listening.
fix: Check whether the Service exists: kubectl get svc inventory-db -n pfa-lab
If it is missing, deploy the database and its Service named inventory-db in pfa-lab.

If the database runs in another namespace or under a different name, set the DB_HOST env var on container api to the correct name (e.g. inventory-db.<namespace>) and roll out: kubectl set env deployment/stock-api -n pfa-lab DB_HOST=<correct-host>
Leave the readiness probe unchanged: it is correctly keeping traffic away until the database resolves.

results.cause: The readiness probe is configured as "HTTP /ready port=http", but the app only serves /healthz: the container creates only /www/healthz and logs "catalog-api listening on :80, health at /healthz". httpd returns 404 for /ready (event: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404", x44263). The port is correct (http=80/TCP); only the path is wrong.
fix: Change spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].readinessProbe.httpGet.path from /ready to /healthz in deployment/catalog-api, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch deployment catalog-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/healthz"}]'
Alternatively, if /ready must stay, make the app serve it (e.g. add `echo ok > /www/ready` to the container args).
After the rollout, confirm with kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/catalog-api.

results.cause: The app spends 45 seconds replaying its journal before it starts httpd on port 80 (log: "ledger-api replaying journal, this takes about 45 seconds", then "sleep 45"). The liveness probe starts after initialDelaySeconds=2 and checks every periodSeconds=3 with failureThreshold=2, and there is no startupProbe. Nothing is listening on :80 yet, so it gets "connect: connection refused" and the kubelet kills the container after roughly 8 seconds. The "listening on :80" line never appears in the logs. The kill shows as exit code 137 even though the app did not crash. The port (http=80) and path (/healthz) are correct.
fix: Add a startupProbe on the api container that covers the 45s startup with margin, e.g. startupProbe: httpGet {path: /healthz, port: http}, periodSeconds: 5, failureThreshold: 18 (about 90s). Keep the existing livenessProbe; it only starts running after the startupProbe succeeds.
Alternatively, raise livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to at least 60 (a startupProbe is preferred because it adapts if the replay gets faster or slower).

Optionally add a readinessProbe on /healthz port http so traffic is only sent once httpd is up, and set resource requests (the pod is currently BestEffort) so a slow node does not stretch startup further.
Apply the change with kubectl -n pfa-lab edit deployment/ledger-api (or update the manifest) and watch the rollout with kubectl -n pfa-lab rollout status deployment/ledger-api.

results.cause: The liveness probe targets "HTTP /healthz port=8080", but the app runs "httpd -f -p 80", logs "inventory-api listening on :80" and declares only port http=80/TCP. Nothing listens on 8080, so each probe gets "dial tcp 10.244.0.12:8080: connect: connection refused". After failure_threshold 2 the kubelet kills the container, which shows as exit code 137 even though the app never crashed.
fix: In statefulset/inventory-api, set spec.template.spec.containers[name=api].livenessProbe.httpGet.port to 80 or to the named port "http" instead of 8080, e.g. kubectl -n pfa-lab patch statefulset inventory-api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/httpGet/port","value":"http"}]'
Keep path /healthz. The startup command already writes /www/healthz, so it will return 200 on port 80.
Make sure the pod is recreated, and delete inventory-api-0 if needed. Then confirm the restart count stops increasing and no new Unhealthy events appear.
